message.content: We spent the morning on the vector index readiness poll in the indexing pipeline. The symptom was a search that answered with an empty parents list right after an ingest, even though the memory collection clearly held the child chunks with their embeddings. My hunch is that Atlas reports the index as existing long before mongot has finished syncing it, so the poll declares ready while the first query still sees nothing. Can you walk the readiness helper with me and tell me whether the catalogue entry exposes a queryable flag we can wait on instead of the plain existence check we use today?

content.text: Reading the helper now. The poll loops over the search index catalogue and returns as soon as an entry with the configured name appears, which is exactly the race you describe: the entry exists in the catalogue during the build, and only the queryable field flips once mongot can serve it. The fix is to wait for queryable, raise on a FAILED status so a broken build never reads as an empty memory, and fail open after five minutes so a slow local container cannot wedge the pipeline forever. Local mongot reports neither field, so an entry without status and without queryable has to be read as ready or the local stack would hang.

I applied that change and the readiness line now names the status it waited on. A still building index therefore surfaces as a text only search mode with one caveat line rather than as an empty result, which is the behaviour we wanted: degraded is visible, not silently broken.

message.content: That matches what I saw in the logs. Please keep the five minute fail open bound as a constant rather than a config knob, and record the reasoning in the architecture decision record so nobody turns it into a tunable by accident.
